## Background

Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a group of genetic disorders in which red
blood cells contort into a sickle shape. Symptoms of SCD include anemia
(caused by misshapen cells dying early) as well as pain, infection, and
stroke (caused by sickle cells blocking blood flow). There is some
evidence that exposure to air pollution aggravates vaso-occlusion and
pain in SCD patients.

A hematologist at Duke wants to study the associations between various
air pollutants and SCD in Durham County, North Carolina. She provides
data on health system utilization (i.e., emergency department visits,
hospitalizations, etc.) for SCD and you obtain air pollution data from
the EPA. The pollutant data are raw measurements taken from the air
pollution monitor at the RDU airport. 

```{r data-processing, include=FALSE}
# Custom function reads in data and performs cleaning; set O3 units to ppb
aq18 <- clean_aq_data("data/AQ_2018.csv", units_o3 = "ppb")
aq19 <- clean_aq_data("data/AQ_2019.csv", units_o3 = "ppb")
aq20 <- clean_aq_data("data/AQ_2020.csv", units_o3 = "ppb")

# Combine data from each year into one dataset
aq_full <- bind_rows(aq18, aq19, aq20)
```

## Plots 
```{r plot 1, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.5, out.width="100%"}
# Create data frame with monthly summary statistics for CO and O3
monthly_summary <- aq_full |>
  # Select date and pollutant concentrations
  select(Date, co_max8hr, o3_max8hr) |>

  # Create column extracting month from date
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      # Get three letter abbreviation format for month
      month.abb[lubridate::month(Date)],
      levels = month.abb
    )
  ) |>

  # Reshape pollutants into one column
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(co_max8hr, o3_max8hr),
    names_to = "pollutant",
    values_to = "concentration"
  ) |>

  # Group by pollutant and calendar month
  group_by(pollutant, month) |>

  # Calculate monthly statistics
  summarise(
    mean = mean(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    count = sum(!is.na(concentration)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>

  # Calculate lower and upper bounds for each month
  mutate(
    LB = mean - 1.96 * SD / sqrt(count),
    UB = mean + 1.96 * SD / sqrt(count)
  )

# Plot monthly average concentrations for CO and O3
ggplot(monthly_summary, aes(x = month, y = mean, color = pollutant)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = LB, ymax = UB)) +
  facet_wrap(~ pollutant,
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 1,
    labeller = as_labeller(c(
      co_max8hr = "CO (ppm)",
      o3_max8hr = "O3 (ppb)"
    ))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Plot 1: Monthly Mean CO and O3 Concentrations",
    subtitle = "Pooled Daily Measurements, Jan 2018– Apr 2020",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean Concentration",
    color = "Pollutant"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      co_max8hr = "#7570B3",
      o3_max8hr = "#1B9E77"
    ),
    labels = c(
      co_max8hr = "CO",
      o3_max8hr = "O3"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )

```


To account for large difference in scales, I chose to display mean concentrations of CO (ppm) and O3 (ppb) with independent y-axis scales. This ensures patterns in both pollutant concentrations are readable. It is also worth noting that because data collection stopped in April of 2020, monthly means for January-April are based on 3 years of data while May-December are based on only 2.  
&nbsp;

```{r Plot 2, fig.width=7}
# Create data frame of average daily PM2.5 by month and year
monthly_pm <- aq_full |>
  # Create year and month variables
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(Date),
    month = factor(
      month.abb[lubridate::month(Date)],
      levels = month.abb
    )
  ) |>

  # Group observations by year and month
  group_by(year, month) |>

  # Calculate monthly mean PM2.5 concentration
  summarise(
    mean_pm = mean(pm25_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Create line plot of monthly means by year

ggplot(monthly_pm, aes(x = month,
                       y = mean_pm,
                       color = as.factor(year),
                       group = year)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Plot 2: Monthly Mean PM2.5 Concentrations by Year",
    subtitle = "2018–2020",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean PM2.5 Concentration (µg/m³ LC)",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0)
  ) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5)
```

It appears CO and O3 concentrations are inversely related, with CO levels reaching a peak in summer months and O3 levels peaking in winter months. The summary tables show 2020 has a high maximum PM2.5 concentration and a low maximum O3 concentration compared to previous years; the low maximum O3 value may be explained by the lack of data for May-December, since O3 levels previously peaked in June. There does not appear to be a clear annual pattern in monthly PM2.5 concentration levels.
